transcript.text: Hi everyone, I've called this package-lock meeting to finalize delivery of the live-concert documentary. As a reminder, the streaming platform has requested a worldwide 68-minute master for delivery this Friday, and the film is currently assembled at 68 minutes. Before I can authorize delivery, I need to review four items with each of you: release territory, running time, credits, and approval requirements. I'd like each of the three responsible production leads to report any outstanding requirement in their area. Once all three of you have responded, I'll issue the formal settlement action and authorization decision right here in this meeting. Let's start — could each lead please confirm your area and report any outstanding requirements?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue. I reviewed the executed music license this morning, and the featured song permits digital streaming only in the United States and Canada — not worldwide. The license also requires a cue sheet to be delivered with the authorized master. I have not yet entered those limits in the release tracker, so the tracker does not reflect this territorial restriction.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue on my end. I checked the archive-footage license exhibit with the post house today, and it confirms that the finished program may not exceed exactly 52 minutes. Our current assembly is 68 minutes, which means it cannot be delivered under the existing footage license. I have not yet updated the runtime sheet to reflect this restriction.
